actionResult.summary: 按 159→169 完整审查链复核 168 Apply：160/162 的 Explore findings 已在 164 收敛，166 Proposal 已批准；168 的 strict identity、checkpoint-time Owner authorization、read-only checkpoint handoff 与主要 verification 均成立。但 bounded legacy cutover 仍存在一个 Author blocker：strict E2 anchor 可被 subject-only consumer 绕过，且可被未来重复 E2 checkpoint 向前重定义，导致 post-anchor malformed checkpoint 被追溯性 legacy-admit。

reviewFindings.title: bounded legacy cutover anchor can be bypassed or moved forward
reviewFindings.problem: The Apply implements the F1 legacy exemption by matching the E2 change identity instead of binding one stable original strict cutover boundary. readGitBoundarySummaries also special-cases an E2 subject-only candidate as a checkpoint fact. As a result, one consumer can activate post-E2 behavior from a non-strict checkpoint, while FormalFactReader can later select a newer duplicate E2 checkpoint and retroactively extend the legacy-readable window past the original strict anchor.
reviewFindings.invariant: Only checkpoints strictly before the original strict-admitted E2 cutover may use the bounded legacy read path; the anchor itself and every descendant/future checkpoint must remain strict, and no consumer may treat a subject-only E2 candidate as the activation checkpoint.
evidence: src/facts/git-boundary-reader.ts:139-157 explicitly admits the migration E2 changeId through readGitBoundarySummaries even when formalIdentityValid is false; src/services/b1-run-execution-service.ts:665-671 consumes those summaries to activate the post-E2 writer.

Disposable Git fixture with Delivery Start + subject-only E2 checkpoint produced a change-checkpoint fact from readGitBoundarySummaries, proving the special case is executable rather than dead compatibility code.
src/facts/formal-fact-reader.ts:592-605 uses checkpointCandidates.find(...) for the E2 changeId; git log --all is newest-first, so a later duplicate strict E2 checkpoint becomes anchorCandidate.

Disposable Git fixture with original strict E2 anchor, then a subject-only F1 checkpoint, then a later duplicate strict E2 checkpoint caused readFormalFactSnapshot to admit the intervening subject-only F1 checkpoint as legacy, proving the exemption can expand beyond the original cutover.
Current exact base e182492181166ef00b8546923f1ce6ad168564f7 already contains the legitimate strict E2 checkpoint, so the required cutover can be fixed without rewriting historical Git.
reviewFindings.impact: A malformed post-cutover checkpoint can be interpreted as sufficient E2 activation by the writer path, and a future duplicate E2 checkpoint can retroactively grandfather post-cutover subject-only history. That breaks F1 strict checkpoint authority, makes the legacy exemption non-monotonic, and can let lifecycle/read behavior depend on future Git additions.
reviewFindings.requiredOutcome: Bind the migration cutover to a stable strict E2 boundary and make all consumers respect that same strict activation invariant. Remove the subject-only E2 checkpoint exception from any current checkpoint fact/activation surface. Ensure later same-change commits cannot move the cutover forward (for example by deterministically selecting/pinning the original strict E2 anchor or failing closed on ambiguity). Preserve read-only compatibility only for true ancestors of that original anchor and keep the current base e182 strict transition valid.
acceptance: A subject-only E2 checkpoint is not returned/consumed as a current formal activation checkpoint by readGitBoundarySummaries or isPostE2ThreeFileWriterActive.
After an original strict E2 anchor exists, adding a later strict E2 checkpoint cannot make any descendant of the original anchor eligible for legacy checkpoint admission.
The real e182 strict E2 checkpoint still activates the prospective three-file writer and true pre-E2 historical checkpoints remain readable without history rewrite.
Fresh/downstream repositories remain strict by default and no new Delivery-local or subject-only fallback is introduced.
Regression tests cover both counterexamples: subject-only E2 activation and later duplicate E2 with an intervening malformed post-anchor checkpoint.
